title: The Panama Cafe on 58th Street: Benny Tallinger, Jerry Wilson and the show
summary: After Casino Gardens she sang in the show at the Panama Cafe; she names the boss, pianist-arranger Jerry Wilson and fellow performers.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Do you remember what the, what, uh, you did after Casino Gardens?
Well, yes. When I left Casino Gardens, I went to the Panama Cafe. Oh. Yes. Mm-hmm.
Who was there?
Uh, Benny Tallinger was the, was the, uh, boss that run the, Tallinger, run the Panama. Benny Tallinger. Mm-hmm.
Now, is this the 35th? There were people.
That was at 38, I mean, uh, 58th Street.
58th. All right.
Mm-hmm. The Panama, 58th Street. I think it was about three, and the, and the 300 block on 58th Street.
Uh, 300 East.
Mm-hmm.
Yeah. All right.
And, let's see, and, uh, then from there, there was a...
Who was with you at Panama as a musical accompaniment? Do you remember the orchestra or your pianist?

Now, uh, the pianist was, uh, Jerry Wilson. He used to make all my orchestrate, arrange all my orchestrations for me. Jerry Wilson was a pianist, like, you know, pianist. And I don't know who all was in his orchestra. I can't think.
Two or three pieces?
Oh, they must have had four or fives, because that was a pretty good, pretty good-sized nightclub. Mm-hmm.
Did you, uh, uh, perform as a, uh, uh, uh, nightclub act, or were you a singer?
Just a singer. A singer with a band? Single, single, single. In the show. In the show.
Uh-huh. All right. That's what I meant.
Mm-hmm.
In the Panama show. Do you remember any other, uh, performers who, uh, appeared at the Panama while you were there?
Yeah, Marie Claybrook, she was there, and, and, uh, uh, Nadine Douglas. Jimmy White. He, he was, uh, Jimmy White. He was the, uh, producer of the show. Uh-huh.
